texts.title: The Khareef Season in Salalah
texts.body:
[A] Every year, from about late June to September, Salalah changes completely. This season is called the khareef. Monsoon winds bring light rain, thick mist and cool air from the Indian Ocean. The mountains around the city turn green, and waterfalls and streams appear in the valleys. Many people say the weather is beyond anything they expect from Oman.

[B] Thousands of visitors travel to Dhofar during the khareef. Families from other parts of Oman and from Gulf countries come to enjoy the cool weather. Hotels, shops and restaurants become very busy. The festival offers markets, shows and activities for children. Local people work long hours in this demanding season, but many are happy because it is good for business.

[C] The mist also makes driving dangerous. On mountain roads, drivers cannot see far ahead, so they must drive slowly and keep their lights on. The police put up signs and give safety advice. Visitors should not walk near the edge of the wadis, because the water can rise quickly. A reliable weather report is a practical help for anyone planning a trip.

[D] The khareef is important for nature as well. The rain fills the ground with water, and farmers can grow bananas, coconuts and papayas near the coast. Scientists collect data about the rainfall, the plants and the animals. They use special equipment to measure the wind and the moisture in the air. Some visitors leave rubbish in the green valleys, so officials ask people to cut back on plastic and to take their waste home. Everyone can help to keep the season beautiful.

questions.q: The khareef season lasts all year in Salalah.
questions.evidence: from about late June to September
questions.why: The text says the khareef is only from June to September.

questions.q: Many visitors to Dhofar during the khareef come from Gulf countries.
questions.evidence: Families from other parts of Oman and from Gulf countries come to enjoy the cool weather.
questions.why: The text says families come from Gulf countries.

questions.q: Why must drivers go slowly on mountain roads in the khareef?
options: They cannot see far because of the mist.
questions.evidence: On mountain roads, drivers cannot see far ahead, so they must drive slowly and keep their lights on.
questions.why: Mist makes it hard to see ahead.

questions.q: What do officials want visitors to do about plastic?
questions.evidence: officials ask people to cut back on plastic and to take their waste home
questions.why: Cut back on means to use less.
